key_points: Conservative treatment (counselling, exercises, occlusal splint therapy, massage, manual therapy) should be the first-line approach for TMD pain due to low risk of side effects.
Occlusal splints (Michigan-type, repositioning, reflex appliances) are among the most commonly reported conservative treatments for TMD.
Massage therapy is effective in myofascial TMD pain; at least 8 sessions of 30 min twice weekly are recommended.
Laser therapy at 904 nm and 700 Hz frequency is mentioned as a method for treating inflammatory processes in TMD at 30 mm tissue depth.
Pharmacotherapy (NSAIDs, myorelaxants, analgesics, tricyclic antidepressants, benzodiazepines, corticosteroids) is considered complementary rather than primary treatment for TMD.
Botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A) is supported by clinical investigations for disc displacement and bruxism-related myofascial pain.
Arthrocentesis reduces pain and functional impairment more rapidly than conservative treatment, but long-term outcomes are comparable.
Acupuncture shows long-term effectiveness (18–20 years follow-up) for TMD pain management.
In rheumatoid/systemic disorders with TMJ involvement, pharmacotherapy (methotrexate, TNF inhibitors, corticosteroids) plays a primary role.
TENS cannot yet be considered a standard treatment for TMD due to insufficient randomized trial evidence.
Doxycycline (tetracycline) may help prevent condylar resorption by inhibiting matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs).
Surgical TMJ replacement is indicated for severe arthritis, ankylosis, trauma damage, and failed prior joint replacement.

outcomes.measured: Effectiveness of muscular therapy in TMD
outcomes.clinical_significance: Moderate effectiveness; less effective when mouth opening is limited due to muscular or joint pain

outcomes.measured: Arthrocentesis vs conservative treatment for TMJ pain
outcomes.result: Arthrocentesis reduces pain and functional impairment more rapidly; long-term outcomes comparable
outcomes.clinical_significance: Arthrocentesis may be preferred for faster relief but conservative treatment achieves similar long-term results

outcomes.measured: Occlusal splint therapy (SVED appliance) for TMD
outcomes.result: Decreases head and spine pain and disc displacements within 3 weeks; further improvement at 3 months
outcomes.clinical_significance: Clinically meaningful reduction in symptoms and disc displacement
Long-term pain relief, especially combined with dietary changes

notes: This narrative review covers the full spectrum of TMD treatment modalities from conservative to surgical. Laser therapy is mentioned briefly as a method for inflammatory processes (904 nm, 700 Hz, 30 mm depth) without detailed clinical protocol. Multiple drug classes are discussed with specific dosing recommendations. The paper includes a treatment algorithm (Fig. 1) distinguishing reversible vs irreversible TMD.

contraindications: Cryotherapy: high risk of frostbite; cold compresses should not exceed 10–15 min
Partial coverage occlusal splints may alter maxillary-mandibular arch relationship
NSAIDs: risk of hypertension exacerbation and gastrointestinal ulcerations
Massage performed too intensely may increase muscular tonus rather than relieve it
Pharmacotherapy alone (without addressing underlying systemic disease) is insufficient for TMD associated with systemic disorders
adverse_events: NSAIDs: gastrointestinal upset, ulcerations, hypertension exacerbation
Overly intense massage: increased muscular tonus
Corticosteroids: systemic adverse effects when used long-term

perioperative_consideration: Multiple drug classes used in TMD management have perioperative relevance: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and should be managed perioperatively; benzodiazepines cause sedation and interact with anesthetics; doxycycline and methotrexate cause photosensitivity relevant to laser therapy; botulinum toxin injections require careful timing relative to dental procedures; corticosteroids may require stress-dose supplementation for major procedures.
uncertainties: Laser therapy parameters (904 nm, 700 Hz) are mentioned very briefly without specifying power, fluence, application time, or clinical protocol details — insufficient for a full clinical protocol extraction.
The paper does not specify which laser device/brand is used for the 904 nm treatment.
Pulse duration for the 904 nm laser is not reported.
The review includes 66 papers but does not provide a PRISMA flow diagram or formal quality assessment of included studies, limiting methodological rigor assessment.
Dosing recommendations for some drugs (e.g., orphenadrine) are not fully specified in the paper.

protocols.name: Terapia con láser de baja intensidad para procesos inflamatorios en ATM (904 nm)
protocols.purpose: Tratamiento de procesos inflamatorios en la articulación temporomandibular mediante láser de baja intensidad a 904 nm, con penetración de hasta 30 mm en tejido, para alivio del dolor y reducción de la inflamación articular.
critical_notes: ⚠️ Este protocolo es de carácter teórico/revisión. Los parámetros clínicos completos (potencia, fluencia, tiempo de aplicación, número de sesiones) no están especificados en el paper original. Basado en: Wieckiewicz et al. (2015).
El paper menciona únicamente longitud de onda (904 nm) y frecuencia (700 Hz) como referencia a un método que 'ha ganado popularidad'; no constituye un protocolo clínico completo.

El documento presenta esta técnica como una opción entre múltiples modalidades fisioterapéuticas para TMD; existen alternativas con mecanismos de acción diferentes que pueden ser apropiadas según el caso clínico.
La profundidad de penetración de 30 mm mencionada corresponde a características del láser de 904 nm (semiconductor/diodo pulsado), no a una instrucción de aplicación clínica.
indications: Enfermedades reumáticas inflamatorias con afectación de ATM
protocols.evidence_level: Bajo — revisión narrativa. El paper menciona el método brevemente sin parámetros clínicos completos ni estudios propios. No hay RCTs con protocolos estandarizados reportados en este documento.
